sources.title: NGSS MS-LS1-1: Conduct an investigation to provide evidence that living things are made of cells; either one cell or many different numbers and types of cells

note.text: Carry a microscope with one hand under the base and the other on the arm.
The arm holds the tube and lenses steady above the stage.
Light travels up the tube from the specimen to your eye.

steps.title: Eyepiece
steps.instruction: Trace the eyepiece at the top.

note.text: You look through the eyepiece. Its lens, the ocular lens, usually magnifies 10 times (10×).

steps.title: Objective lenses
steps.instruction: Trace the turning nosepiece and its three objective lenses.

note.text: Objective lenses sit close to the specimen. They usually magnify from 4× to 100×. Turn the nosepiece to switch.
The stage holds the slide. Raising or lowering it brings the image into focus.

steps.title: Slide
steps.instruction: Trace the glass slide on the stage.

note.text: The specimen goes on a slide. It must be thin, so light can pass through it.

steps.title: Light
steps.instruction: Trace the light below the stage.

note.text: A bulb below the stage shines light up through the specimen and into the lenses.
note.remember: Light passes up through the specimen.

steps.title: Focus knobs
steps.instruction: Trace the big and small focus knobs.

note.text: Use the big coarse knob with the low-power lenses, and the small fine knob with high power.

steps.title: Name the parts
steps.instruction: Pick the name for each numbered part.

mistakes.Eyepiece: The eyepiece is at the top, where you look. This lens near the slide is an objective.

mistakes.Fine focus knob: The fine focus knob is the smaller one. This big knob is for coarse focusing.

steps.title: Magnification
steps.question: The eyepiece magnifies 10× and the objective lens 40×. How much bigger does the specimen look?

steps.title: Evidence
steps.instruction: Use the microscope as a scientist.
steps.question: You look at a thin slice of onion skin, then a drop of pond water with tiny swimming creatures. What do both show?

options.text: Living things are made of cells: some of many cells, some of just one
options.feedback: Right. The onion is built of many box-shaped cells; each tiny pond creature may be a single cell.

options.text: Only plants are made of cells
options.feedback: The pond creatures are made of cells too. All living things are.

options.text: Cells are big enough to see without a microscope
options.feedback: Most cells are far too small to see with your eyes alone.
Water isn't alive. The living things in it are made of cells.
